projectName: Web Foundation, API Layer, Auth, and Deployment
description: Establish the production architecture for a private web application on top of the existing Python accounting core: a Python API/service layer, stable JSON contracts, lightweight private auth, and deployment posture for PostgreSQL-first self-hosting over Tailscale.

timing.gatingCondition: Proceed after confirming PostgreSQL remains the primary production backend and after agreeing on Python API framework choice.

principles: Python Owns The Domain - no duplication of accounting or tax logic in Node/Express
PostgreSQL First - production web deployment is optimized for the existing PostgreSQL installation
SQLite Supported, Not Primary - retain compatibility for evaluation and low-concurrency installs
Stable JSON Contracts - frontend consumes explicit API models rather than TUI-shaped tables
Private Sovereignty App - auth is mandatory, but optimized for one trusted primary user rather than multi-tenant complexity
TUI Remains Fallback - web work must not degrade the existing TUI operating path

techStack.backendFramework: FastAPI or Flask with explicit service/router separation
techStack.frontend: Express-served static app or React SPA consuming Python JSON endpoints
techStack.testing: pytest for backend contracts + frontend smoke tests
techStack.database: PostgreSQL primary, SQLite supported via existing DatabaseBackend abstraction
techStack.deployment: Bare metal service on Tailscale network with reverse proxy and systemd/PM2 as appropriate

userStories.title: Select Python web framework and establish application structure
acceptanceCriteria: Choose and document the Python web framework for long-running API service
Create app structure separating routers, request/response models, and domain service adapters
Keep BitcoinAccounts and query classes reusable without moving accounting logic into the web layer
Document how the web app coexists with the TUI and CLI entrypoints
userStories.testStrategy: pytest backend app import and health-route smoke tests

userStories.title: Define canonical JSON models for core resources
acceptanceCriteria: Create stable API response models for portfolio summary, wallet, transaction, gains lot, forecast summary, and integrity finding resources
Normalize field naming away from TUI/table labels such as 'Buy Cur.' and 'Sell Cur.'
Document model versioning strategy and nullability rules
Expose transformed JSON without breaking existing Python domain logic
userStories.testStrategy: pytest model serialization tests with representative fixtures

userStories.title: Implement baseline private auth and session model
acceptanceCriteria: Add login/logout/session endpoints suitable for a private single-operator household app
Support secure password or passphrase authentication with signed session cookie or equivalent token strategy
Protect all non-health API routes by default
Document bootstrap flow for first-time setup on bare metal
userStories.testStrategy: pytest auth route tests and unauthenticated access checks

userStories.title: Production database policy and connection lifecycle
acceptanceCriteria: Define PostgreSQL as recommended production backend for the web app
Implement request-safe backend/session acquisition rather than reusing one long-lived SQLite/TUI-style connection object
Document SQLite support boundaries for low-concurrency deployments
Add configuration notes for connection pooling, transaction handling, and rollback behavior
userStories.testStrategy: pytest backend factory tests for postgres/sqlite selection and per-request lifecycle behavior

userStories.title: Operational deployment and observability baseline
acceptanceCriteria: Document deployment topology for Python API plus frontend on Tailscale-accessible bare metal
Provide health endpoint, startup validation, and structured logging baseline
Document environment variables, secrets handling, and backup expectations
Record known limits and support stance for PostgreSQL vs SQLite in web mode
userStories.testStrategy: Manual deployment checklist + backend health probe verification

high: Treating the TUI orchestration layer as if it were already a stable API could produce brittle web contracts
Reusing a TUI-style shared connection model in a concurrent web server would create correctness and stability risk
medium: Framework choice made too late could create avoidable churn in routing and validation patterns
Overbuilding auth for a private single-user app could slow delivery without adding proportional value
low: The existing Python domain/query core is already mature enough to support an API adapter layer
Tailscale-based private hosting reduces exposure and simplifies first deployment

preFlightChecklist: Confirm Python API framework preference (FastAPI favored for typed JSON contracts)
Confirm PostgreSQL remains the recommended production backend for web mode
Decide whether frontend will be simple server-rendered/static JS or a React SPA
Choose auth bootstrapping approach appropriate for private household use
